about.title: About
about.p1Html: I'm Aron Jake Radam (also known online as ), a Game Developer focusing on gameplay systems, Unity tooling, and technical game design. I got my start in game playtesting and QA at GridLock-Games Studio, testing builds and reporting bugs while collaborating with developers and designers on gameplay feel, balance, and release readiness.
about.haruOriginHtml: Haru means "spring" in Japanese, -chan is a casual Japanese suffix, and Z64 comes from the Nintendo 64 games The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask (my very first Zelda game) and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. It started as a gaming username, and I've kept using it on GitHub and my socials.
about.p2Html: After that, I worked as the sole full-stack engineer at PicStar Software OPC in Las Piñas, Philippines, where I architected PicStar with Flutter and Supabase and shipped it to the Google Play Store. That work sharpened my discipline in live backends, performance, and shipping production software end to end.
about.p3Html: While finishing PicStar, I transitioned into teaching as a College Instructor under the BS EMC (Game Development) program at the University of Caloocan City, where I guide sophomore through senior students across game design theory, prototyping, OOP, game math, AI, networking, and production pipelines. Alongside teaching, I build open-source Unity editor tools and runtime systems to speed up designer and QA workflows.
about.p4Html: I also keep studying game design theory and use AI coding tools in my daily workflow to prototype and debug faster. I'm open to game studio roles, freelance projects, and collaborations.

0.b0: Teach game design theory, rapid prototyping, and production pipelines in Unity and C# to sophomore through senior Bachelor of Science in Entertainment and Multimedia Computing (BS EMC) students, guiding projects from initial mechanics to playable builds.
0.b1: Lead lectures and laboratory sessions on gameplay programming, systems architecture, object-oriented programming (OOP), game mathematics, physics, artificial intelligence (AI), multiplayer networking, and performance optimization to help students turn game design documents into working prototypes.
0.b2: Mentor student teams through code reviews, debugging sessions, and playtest critiques grounded in current game studio practices.

1.b0: Owned end-to-end architecture and engineering of a cross-platform Flutter social mobile application as the sole engineer, building a modular codebase with consistent user interface and user experience (UI and UX).
1.b1: Designed and optimized the Supabase PostgreSQL backend for real-time feeds, ranking queries, location-based filtering, and reduced data egress.
1.b2: Engineered and deployed PicStar to the Google Play Store on October 11, 2026, shipping the Flutter client and Supabase backend into production.

2.b0: Partnered with game developers and designers to test gameplay builds, catch edge-case regressions, and flag usability issues across the release cycle.
2.b1: Logged, reproduced, and tracked bugs in Trello with clear reproduction steps and structured build verification to keep engineering and design fixes moving smoothly.

3.b0: Playtested in-development game builds to uncover gameplay bugs, physics glitches, and mechanics exploits, documenting reproduction steps and verifying fixes across patches.
3.b1: Delivered structured written and verbal feedback on core gameplay loops, pacing, balance, and game feel.

0.degree: Bachelor of Science in Entertainment and Multimedia Computing
0.b0: Relevant Coursework: Game Design and Development, Advanced Game Design, Game Programming 1–3, Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Games, Applied Mathematics for Games, Game Networking, and Game Production.
